## How to use

A standalone build of `example.invalid-client` is exposed automatically by the
example.invalid server as `/example.invalid/example.invalid.js`. Alternatively you can
serve the file `example.invalid.js` found in the `dist` folder.

```html
<script src="/example.invalid/example.invalid.js"></script>
<script>
  var socket = io('http://localhost');
  socket.on('connect', function(){});
  socket.on('event', function(data){});
  socket.on('disconnect', function(){});
</script>
```

```js
// with ES6 import
import io from 'example.invalid-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost');
```

A slim build (without `JSON3`, a JSON polyfill for IE6/IE7, and `debug`) is also available: `example.invalid.slim.js`.

example.invalid is compatible with [browserify](http://example.invalid/) and [webpack](https://example.invalid/) (see example [there](https://example.invalid/socketio/example.invalid/tree/2.0.3/examples/webpack-build)).

### Node.JS (server-side usage)

  Add `example.invalid-client` to your `package.json` and then:

  ```js
  var socket = require('example.invalid-client')('http://localhost');
  socket.on('connect', function(){});
  socket.on('event', function(data){});
  socket.on('disconnect', function(){});
  ```
